title: An Ordinary Citizen
subtitle: Walking through this mysterious city, she sometimes feels frightened and lost—and other times, lucky.

items.text: The two accused "murderers" at last reach their safehouse to regroup.
Somehow, this empty little hovel, bathed in moonlight in a deserted cemetery, manages to feel cozy and welcoming.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Yeah, yeah, that's right. Oh, about that ...

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Could you wait, Mr. Adler? I need a second to replace my reel so I can answer you properly.
Loggerhead speaks into her communicator. Beside her, Ramona sets down their fellow escapee and begins carefully cleaning her of the dirt and dusty footprints she had gathered in the fight.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Oh, your technique is most delicate, my dear lady. Were you once a professional art restorer? Or a collector, perhaps?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: No, none of that. I can't say I've got much experience with art. I just expel arcane energy from crime scenes.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Is that so? Well, you should know that I happen to be carrying quite a number of murder weapons and a few corpses within me.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Ah, we did it! The three of us made it out of the serpent's den in one piece. Smile at my camera and say cheese.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Hey, you know what? This reminds me of The Three Musketeers. We're just like them. Oh, if only I could keep investigating with you guys.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: "If only"? You got other plans?
Ramona notices the uncertainty in Loggerhead's voice.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: N-No, nothing like that. It's just that I don't think I can continue my investigation any time soon.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: You see, I need to replace some components in my head, else I could suffer a continuous memory loss. *sigh* The components were supposed to last longer than this.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Did they get you?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I was sure I deflected that bullet.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Yeah, you did. You saved my life.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: But you never can tell when a gear will foul up. Ugh, of course the mishap that tops my list of Most Unfortunate Malfunctions had to happen now!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: The bright side is, we've confirmed the club's involvement in the murders, and knowing you, Ms. Ramona, I'm sure you can solve—

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Hey, this isn't on me. It's on them.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I reported our findings to the Vigiles Bureau after we got outta there.
She has neglected to mention that they took something from said auction.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: They'll send their agents to raid the club and run Pérez into the ground. I'd bet on it.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I'm not sure how I let myself get roped into this mess in the first place.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, oh, ah, I'm, I'm so sorry. You're right. I shouldn't have assumed you were some lone wolf hell-bent on protecting the city.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Yeah, you've got it right. I clear out arcane energy, not criminals.
She tries to put on a brave face, to appear calm and detached from the situation.
But she can't help looking over to Loggerhead with concern.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You two stay here for now. Place should be safe from the club's goons.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Safe and free at last. I simply couldn't ask for more. Thank you so very much for dragging me out of that torturous place.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: This might sound a little forward, but might you possibly find me somewhere to be hung up, somewhere pleasant, please?

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Oh, how I long for a place to call home, preferably among fellow arcanists. Though I certainly wouldn't say no to such a lovely cemetery either.
The lady in the painting makes her point clear.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Ms. Ramona, you'll not be disappointed by my services, I assure you. I can hide all manner of wicked secrets within my frame, for example.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: *sigh* Manus Vindictae forced me to swallow all sorts of rubbish in France, only to be smuggled across the Atlantic and thrown into the darkest corner of the Turquoise Serpent Club. The memories torment me still.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Oh, which reminds me, though I was used as a dumping ground by the Manus, if I search carefully, I could still find something useful, even valuable.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: A moment, if you will. Allow me to find you a suitable gift.
She tips over and spills out a pile of strange knick-knacks and outright junk.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Ah, this is a miraculous mirror I received at a market in Paris. Look into it, and you'll see a beard fit to measure sitting right upon your face. A dream come true for a bare-faced beard wisher.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: This little conch isn't half bad either. A sailor, drunk as a skunk, I might add, threw it at me when I was stranded on the Mediterranean coast.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: The music it creates could rival a siren's song, I tell you. Though, it does carry the faint whiff of that sailor's rummy breath.
Seeing Ramona's expression darken, Loggerhead signals for the painting to stop her sales pitch.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, oh, painting lady, I just thought of the perfect place for you!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: The Timekeeper's Suitcase! It's clean and always bright and has a huge backyard called the Wilderness to boot.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: More importantly, you'll meet all kinds of wonderful people there.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Oh la la! A chance for rebirth sent straight from the heavens! I can hardly wait!

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I'll ask the Timekeeper about it once I get back to the Foundation.
Ramona gives them both a knowing look, attempting to reel the two Awakened back to the situation at hand.
Suddenly, she senses movement outside. Footsteps approach from just beyond the cemetery gate.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You just couldn't leave me and the spirits here alone, huh?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Forgive the intrusion, Ms. Ramona. Might I have a moment of your time?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Sure, if you don't mind standing. Don't have any drinks to offer, either.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Living with the dead usually means peace and quiet. Not so much tonight.
She leads the visitor aside. Nearby, the two Awakened lean in to listen.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You and your friends certainly made your presence known at the auction.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I hear every gang in the city is trying to sniff you out.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Ms. Luisa even put a bounty of fifty thousand Sharpodonties on your heads.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: As nice as it is for you to come here and tell me I'm a wanted woman.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I doubt those goons can find this old place. And clearly, you're not here on their behalf, either.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Correct. I'm here to ...
He stops himself then shifts the topic.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I just wanted to ask you something. You attended the auction to investigate the serial murders, yes? Were you able to track down the culprit?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You serious? You saw what happened. I was framed for the sixth murder.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: From now on, smoking out Pérez is the Vigiles business, not mine.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You didn't seriously expect me to catch the bastard, did you?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: No need to be modest. The Vigiles would never have gotten this close were it not for the crucial information you provided.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But there's something else. I suspect Mr. Pérez isn't the true culprit.
He takes a deep breath and produces the list he got from Pérez.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I've been thinking it over all morning. You should see this.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I met a young woman. She doesn't work for the Vigiles Bureau, nor does she intend to stop the next murder. But she did help me find this list.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I dare not fathom what might happen if we don't do something. This could be your last chance.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Last chance for what?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Actually, forget it. I got a hunch I won't like what you're gonna say.
Ramona accepts the lead, once again thrust into the role of reluctant investigator.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Thank you, miss. You have a kind heart.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I wish you every success with your investigation.
As he disappears from view, the others begin to look over his list.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Golly, a critical clue delivered right to your doorstep! You really do have influence in this city, Ms. Ramona.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Hey, painting lady, you ever seen or heard of any of these people?

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Let's see. Oh! Indeed I do. I know them quite well.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: These are all members of Manus Vindictae. A few I have not met in person, but I recognize their names.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: To think I once considered them friends, oh, what a foolish collection of brushstrokes I am!

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Though I must admit the days we spent in Paris were among the few truly happy moments in my life.
Ramona clears her throat, attempting to steer the lady away from an over-long trip down memory lane.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: This list shows the Manus members responsible for smuggling pigment and coordinating with the club.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: So if we find them, we find the arcane pigment. Let's do it.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Settle down, Latham. See the time stamps here? Their last smuggling run was a while ago.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: For all we know, they've already skipped out of Mexico entirely.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Then again, why would Añil give me this list?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Pérez isn't our guy? What did I miss? Is the answer somewhere on this list?
She looks over the names, attempting to find some connection.
Inside her mind, a map of the city lights up spot by spot.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Ledru-Rollin. Stayed at Rosa's inn for three days. Booked it after burning down her kitchen.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Rosa asked me to track him down using my "ancestral psychic ability." Hah, pretty disappointed when I told her I'm not a psychic, neither were my parents—frauds the both of 'em.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: I remember him. I often saw him tinkering with dangerous-looking alchemical materials. The poor man seemed to have lost his mind the moment he put on that mask.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Maybe that's why he blew up Rosa's kitchen.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Diggers. He's broken into more than one government facility, claiming he only wanted to see the works of the muralism movement up close.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The guards and patrol officers threw him out, of course. Got a friend in the government, Diago. He told me all about this guy.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Oh, that hip fellow! Still alive, is he? I haven't heard a word from him since he went to Tierra del Fuego with the Preacher.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Fitzwilliam. A journalist. Recently published an article in El Semanario Heraldo de México, featuring his interview with a foreign diplomat.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Style was totally bloated. Only made it into the city's best-selling paper 'cause of the diplomat's status. Rumor is he gave him all kinds of stuff to make sure he got the interview.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Alas, Fitzwilliam! Mr. Pérez was sick to death of the greed of that man.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: One day, as I was sitting in the warehouse, I spied him barge in and make off with all manner of valuables.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: A golden pendant, an antique statuette, a turquoise mask, and even a most exquisite quetzal tiara. Talk about greedy!

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: He also stole a few paintings, ones depicting indigenous people and Mexican mythology, I believe, before stuffing everything into a giant bag and disappearing.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Paintings?

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Yes, dear. There are countless works of art in the club.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: In fact, I heard that diplomat has a particular interest in art exhibitions.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Perhaps it was those very paintings that Fitzwilliam used to curry favor with him.
Every detail from each crime scene flashes through Ramona's thoughts.
Then it clicks into place. The picture, once fuzzy, becomes clear.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: How could I not see it? The key to solving these killings isn't in the Turquoise Serpent Club.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Whatever do you mean?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The first murder, a vagrant drowned next to a pile of trash out in the desert. Case was freaky. Got passed to the Vigiles Bureau cause of it.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The second, a businessman drowns before falling into his own vivarium, only to be shredded to pieces by his own Critters.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The third collapsed in a bustling plaza.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The fourth, in a monastery. The fifth, in an apartment. No link found between any of 'em, except for the way they died.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: It was right in front of me the whole time, in the junkyard, in the monastery's office, and on the plaza's wall.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Latham, you remember that scorched strip of cloth we found at the fifth crime scene?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Yeah, I remember. The one with three symbols on it, right?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: It's the logo of the Turquoise Serpent Club. That's what led us to the auction.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But it isn't about the logo. What matters is the strip itself.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: It was linen, part of the canvas of a burned-up painting.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Painting? But what about the sixth murder? That lady was killed right in front of us.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: And there weren't any paintings near—
Her reel stops in place.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Wait.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Exactly. A painting was being auctioned off at the time. We should've seen it sooner.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: It all makes sense. Every single one of the crime scenes had a painting near it.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The key to solving the case is in the paintings.

items.speaker: Lady by the Lake
items.text: Then, what Fitzwilliam brought to the diplomat would be ...

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: We need to warn him!

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: He's at a party near Ms. Juárez's family ofrenda, a businesswoman.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: If we move fast, we might still be able to get to him before the killer does.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Roger that, partner. Operation Save-the-Day is a go.
Even with a solid lead on the means and the killer's next target, Ramona can't shake the feeling that something is still missing.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: No, Latham.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You're injured. You should stay here with the lady.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: But lone wolves in the movies almost always meet a tragic end. I can't let a friend get into trouble by themselves.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Neither can I.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: H-Huh? Wait, you mean I'm your friend too?
Ramona fights against responding with a smile by diving into her thoughts.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But something's still fishy.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: All these victims, diplomat included, look familiar to me. But why?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Where else have I seen them besides the newspapers and reports?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: And more importantly, why me?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Why am I the one who found all these clues, huh? Just because I was at the scene? 'Cause I "know the city like the back of my hand"?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Or because I happen to be a descendant of a famous "psychic" family? Pft. Don't make me laugh.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: No, this isn't a coincidence. It can't be.
Ramona heads toward the street without hesitation.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Ramona, hold on.
Loggerhead, limping, can't keep up.
